chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he was asked about the man who swears with a vow, and his intention in his oath which he had sworn upon is one Dirham or less. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he does not dedicate it for Allah, then it is nothing.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a vow made with a small amount of money if it is not dedicated for Allah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a vow (nadhr) involving a small monetary value, such as a dirham, is legally void if it lacks the specific intention of being dedicated for the sake of Allah. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of vows hinges on the sincerity of the intent (niyyah) rather than the material magnitude of the pledged item. It highlights the distinction between casual oaths and binding religious commitments in personal worship.
